sub: Named after “the city” (al-balad), Makkah, in ayah 1
theme: Man is created for struggle, and given eyes, speech and two clear roads. The steep road of freeing, feeding and faith leads to the right; denial leads to a Fire shut tight.
story: Revealed early in Makkah, when the Quraysh had turned hard against the Prophet ﷺ. They would not even hunt in the sacred city, yet they treated harming him there as lawful.

A strong, proud man of Quraysh, reportedly Abū al-Ashuddayn, thought no one could overpower him. He boasted of the heaps of wealth he had spent against the Prophet ﷺ, and reportedly lied about the amount.
The surah answers him. Life is struggle, Allah sees everything, and wealth only counts when it climbs the steep road: freeing slaves and feeding the hungry, with faith.

sections.title: By Makkah: man is born to toil, yet boasts, forgetting Allah sees
sections.meaning: Allah swears by Makkah, where the Prophet ﷺ lives, and by Adam and his children: man is created into kabad, toil and hardship. Yet the proud man thinks no one can overpower him, brags about the wealth he spent, and forgets that Allah sees him.
points: By this city, and you, the Prophet ﷺ, are ḥill in it
By the father and his children
Thinks no one can beat him, brags of wealth, forgets he is seen
sections.matters: It sets the ground rule for the whole surah: this life is struggle, not rest. Then it exposes the proud man who trusts his strength and his spending, and reminds him that Allah is watching.
sections.story: Reportedly about Abū al-Ashuddayn, a strongman of Quraysh who dared anyone to pull a leather hide from under his feet. He boasted of wealth spent against the Prophet ﷺ. Another report names al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah.
explained: Allah swears by al-balad, Makkah. The Prophet ﷺ is ḥill in it: either he lives there, or his enemies treat harming him there as lawful, or it would be made lawful for him to fight in it, as happened for one hour at the Conquest.

By Adam and his children, man is created fī kabad. From the womb to birth, weaning, earning a living, old age, death and the Hereafter, it is struggle. Yet the proud man thinks no one can touch him. He brags, “I have burned through heaps of wealth.” Does he think no one saw it?
teaches: Life is struggle, so struggle for what lasts.
Strength and money don’t put you beyond Allah’s reach.
Allah sees how you earn and how you spend.
Spending to show off is wealth destroyed.
sections.hook: Three oaths (city, father, child) lead to the answer in ayah 4. Then the same question, a-yaḥsabu an…, opens ayah 5 and ayah 7, with the boast in between.

sections.title: The proud man was given eyes, tongue, lips, and shown two roads
sections.meaning: Allah reminds the proud man what he was given: two eyes to see, a tongue and two lips to speak, and a clear view of the two roads, good and evil. Gifts like these call for thanks, not for using them to disobey.
points: Did We not give him two eyes?
And a tongue and two lips?
And show him the two high roads?
sections.matters: It answers “Does he think no one sees him?” with his own face. The One who gave him eyes is watching him, and He made right and wrong clear, so the choice is now his.
sections.story: No specific incident. It continues the reply to the proud man of section 1.
explained: Two eyes to see with. A tongue to say what is inside him. Two lips to help him speak and eat, and to make his face beautiful. The lips also cover the tongue, so he can close them on what is forbidden.

An-najdayn are two high, clear roads: good and evil. Allah made both plain to him. These are blessings for this world and for his faith, and they call for thanks and obedience. But this man did not respond.
teaches: Your eyes and tongue are gifts to use for good.
Guard your tongue; your lips were made to close.
Right and wrong were made clear; the choice is yours.
sections.hook: Three short questions of gifts, all in pairs: ʿaynayn (two eyes), shafatayn (two lips), najdayn (two roads). Only lisān, the tongue, is single.

sections.title: The steep pass: freeing slaves, feeding orphans; deniers get a sealed Fire
sections.meaning: Yet he did not force his way up al-ʿaqabah, the steep pass. It is freeing a slave, or feeding in a day of hunger an orphan relative or a poor person in the dust, while being a believer who urges patience and mercy. Such people are on the right; deniers are on the left, under a sealed Fire.
points: He did not take on the steep pass. What is it?
Feeding in famine: an orphan relative, a poor person in the dust
Then believing, and urging patience and mercy
People of the right; people of the left under a sealed Fire
sections.matters: This is the real answer to the boaster. He wasted heaps of wealth on pride; the true climb is spending on those in need, with faith, among people who urge patience and mercy. It ends by splitting people into two companies.
sections.story: No specific incident. It continues the reply: this is how the boaster should have spent his wealth, instead of spending it against the Prophet ﷺ.
explained: Iqtiḥām is forcing your way through something hard. The ʿaqabah is a steep mountain pass, a picture of fighting your own desires to do good. Its steps: freeing a slave, or helping one buy freedom, and feeding someone on a day of hunger.

Best of all, an orphan who is also a relative, or a poor person clinging to the dust. These deeds count with faith, among believers who urge ṣabr and marḥamah. They are the people of the right. Those who reject Allah’s signs are the people of the left, with a Fire shut over them.
teaches: Real generosity helps those in most need, not your image.
Giving to a needy relative counts twice.
Good deeds need faith behind them.
Don’t only be patient and kind: urge others to be.
Doing good is uphill, so climb anyway.
sections.hook: Wa mā adrāka (12) opens a list joined by aw, “or”: freeing, feeding, orphan, poor. Thumma (17) adds faith. It ends with a mirror pair: maymanah (18) and mashʾamah (19).

groups.text: Allah swears by Makkah, where the Prophet ﷺ lives, and by Adam and his children.
Man is created into toil and hardship.
The proud man thinks no one can overpower him, brags of wealth he spent, and forgets Allah sees him.
Allah gave him two eyes, a tongue and two lips, and showed him the two roads of good and evil.
But he did not take on the steep pass. And what is the steep pass?
Freeing a slave, or feeding in a time of hunger an orphan relative or a poor person in the dust.
And being a believer who urges patience and mercy. These are the people of the right.
Those who reject Allah’s signs are the people of the left, under a Fire shut tight.

1.explain: Lā uqsimu: the lā either rejects the disbelievers’ false claims before the oath, or simply adds weight. Al-balad is Makkah, the sacred city.

2.explain: Ḥill: either you live in this city; or they think harming you here is lawful, though they won’t even hunt in it; or fighting in it will be made lawful for you, as it was for one hour at the Conquest.

3.explain: Wālid wa mā walad: Adam and all his children. Other views: Ibrāhīm and his children, or every father and child.

4.explain: Kabad: toil and hardship, from the womb through birth, weaning, earning a living, old age, death and the Hereafter. This is what the oaths lead to. Another view: created upright and strong.

5.explain: Does the proud man think his strength and wealth put him beyond anyone’s reach, and that no one will ask how he earned and spent it? Allah has full power over him.
5.why: Reportedly about Abū al-Ashuddayn (Usayd ibn Kildah), a strongman of Quraysh. He stood on a leather hide and offered a reward to anyone who could pull it from under him; it would tear first. Another report names al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah.

6.explain: Ahlaktu mālan lubadā: “I have burned through heaps of wealth.” Spending on desires and sin is called destroying wealth, since it brings back only regret. Spending for Allah is a trade that multiplies.
6.why: Reportedly he boasted of spending great wealth against the Prophet ﷺ, and was lying. Another report names al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir ibn Nawfal, who complained his wealth had gone on expiations and spending since he became Muslim.

7.explain: Does he think no one saw him: how much he really spent, where he got it and where it went? Allah saw it all and recorded every deed, small and large.

8.explain: Did We not give him two eyes to see with? The question makes him admit blessings he uses every moment.

9.explain: …and a tongue to express what is inside him, and two lips to help him speak and eat, and to beautify his face. The lips cover the tongue: close them on what is forbidden.

10.explain: An-najdayn: two high, clear roads, good and evil. Allah made both plain so man can choose. Another view: the mother’s two breasts.

11.explain: Fa-lā iqtaḥama al-ʿaqabah: he did not force his way up the steep pass, because he followed his desires. Or: why didn’t he spend his wealth on this instead?

12.explain: Wa mā adrāka: a question that shows how great the pass is, and then Allah explains it. Other views: a steep climb in Hell, or the bridge over it, crossed through obedience.

13.explain: Fakku raqabah: freeing a neck from slavery, either freeing a slave or helping one pay for freedom. Freeing a Muslim captive is even more deserving. Whoever frees a slave is freed from the Fire, limb for limb.

14.explain: Or feeding someone on a day of masghabah, severe hunger, when food is scarce and the need is greatest.

15.explain: An orphan who is also a relative (dhā maqrabah). Charity to a relative counts twice: as charity and as keeping family ties.

16.explain: Or a miskīn dhā matrabah: so poor he clings to the dust, with no home to shelter him. The poorer the person, the greater the reward.

17.explain: Thumma: on top of these deeds he is a believer, since they only benefit with faith. Believers urge each other to ṣabr, in obedience and hardship, and to marḥamah, mercy to all people.

18.explain: Those are aṣḥāb al-maymanah, the people of the right: they receive their record in the right hand and are the people of Paradise.

19.explain: Those who reject Allah’s signs are aṣḥāb al-mashʾamah, the people of the left: they receive their record in the left hand and are the people of the Fire.

20.explain: Nārun muʾṣadah: a Fire closed over them, its doors shut. No light, no gap and no way out, ever.
